- When sentiment is consistently high (>0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day) and sentiment is low (<0.4), likely overreaction; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak.
- In low-sentiment environments (<0.3), model often underestimates downward moves; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for downside risk.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in early 30-day horizon; if 10-day average is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust forecast downward by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is rising (e.g., >0.65) and model forecast is flat or declining, model misses bullish momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- In high-sentiment + high-price environment, model often overcorrects; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.2–0.5% per day after sentiment >0.8.
- If model forecast is >+3% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply “overshoot correction”: subtract 0.5–1.0% from next forecast to avoid overbought bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses tail risk; if sentiment is low and true outcome drops >2% from prior day, add 0.5–1.0% downward buffer to forecast.
